paragraphs.notes: The page body is a single unbroken continuation of a Markush substituent enumeration that starts on an earlier page and continues onto the next: it begins mid-list with no capital-letter sentence start and ends with a comma and no terminating punctuation. There are no [00NN] paragraph markers anywhere in this patent. The only German prose in it is the recurring connective 'gegebenenfalls substituiertes Mono- oder Di...'; everything else is substituent-class names, so the en field is the same list with the German connectives translated and the German chemical prefixes rendered in English orthography (Alkinyl -> alkynyl). Transcribed verbatim per rule 1, so three printed spellings that look like typos are left as printed and NOT corrected: 'Arylalkinyoxycarbonyloxy', 'Heteroarylalkinyoxycarbonyloxy' and 'Heterocyclylalkinyoxycarbonyloxy' all lack the 'l' that the parallel 'Alkinyloxy...' entries carry; each was re-read at 2x magnification to confirm. Also as printed, the '...aminocarbonyloxy' run begins directly at 'Mono- oder Diheteroarylaminocarbonyloxy' with no preceding Mono-/Dialkyl- or Mono-/Diaryl-aminocarbonyloxy members, unlike the parallel '...aminocarbonyl' and '...aminocarbonylamino' runs; that gap is in the original and is not a transcription omission. A small stray ink speck sits above the word 'substituiertes' on the fourth printed line ('Heterocyclylalkinylcarbonyloxy, Aminocarbonyl, gegebenenfalls substituiertes Mono-'); it is scanner dirt, not a character, and obscures nothing. A second faint speck sits in the left margin left of the header, outside the text block.
